case_study_packaging.headline: SaVida Health unlocks $412K in annual savings and 1.5× ROI in just six months with Treya’s strategic sourcing program
case_study_packaging.client_problem_statement: Fresh off an aggressive clinic expansion, SaVida Health’s spend was scattered across dozens of vendors with little central oversight. Council Capital, the PE sponsor, needed rapid margin improvement without disrupting patient care or burdening lean corporate resources. SaVida turned to Treya Partners to capture quick, verifiable savings and to build a scalable procurement foundation.
approach_summary: Analyzed $5.3 million in baseline spend across 10 indirect categories to pinpoint the fastest-payback opportunities.
Renegotiated the incumbent Athena EMR contract, cutting the fee from 4.56 % to 3.40 % and preserving system continuity.
Enrolled SaVida in the Provista GPO, securing national-tier pricing on high-volume medical and office-supply SKUs.
Benchmarked IT hardware pricing and leveraged alternate VAR quotes to drive down unit costs before upcoming clinic openings.
Consolidated fragmented telecom accounts and designed a Comcast managed-services solution to rationalize bandwidth and support future growth.
case_study_packaging.value_delivered_blurb: Treya delivered $412,065 in recurring annual savings—nearly doubling the $210K guarantee and achieving a 23.6 % average reduction across five categories. The flagship $357,889 EMR win was finalized within six months, and an additional $54K is moving through final contracts. Including Treya’s hybrid fee structure, SaVida realized a 1.5× return on investment while also gaining tighter contract terms, centralized spend visibility, and a roadmap for continued cost discipline.
where_we_were_unique: Secured the largest savings from an incumbent EMR provider—avoiding a costly migration and service disruption.
Leveraged deep healthcare GPO expertise to unlock immediate, no-switch discounts on medical and office supplies.
Drove quick wins under an aggressive six-month timeline despite limited internal data and decentralized purchasing.
Maintained clinician and vendor buy-in through a collaborative, hands-on communication strategy that prevented side conversations and pushback.
